# Antikythera — Agentworld Site Copy (2026)

## Bibliographic identity

The live Agentworld landing page (https://agentworld.antikythera.org/), carrying the research-unit self-description and the call for papers for the Agentworld special issue of *Antikythera: Journal for the Philosophy of Planetary Computation* (MIT Press). Local capture at [[symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/antikythera/antikythera-2026-site-copy/antikythera-2026-site-copy.md|antykathera-site-copy]] (working/antykathera-resources/), taken from the official site; live-site spot-check 2026-08-10 confirmed the capture verbatim on the load-bearing passages (preemptive-anthropology definition, MIT Press journal identity, Fall 2026 launch, June 25 call window). Web source: no fixed edition; the accessed date and the live check are the stability record. Content overlaps the Agentworld Brief PDF ([[symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md|bratton-2026-agentworld-brief]]), which remains the primary venue house for argument-facing quotation; this house carries what the PDF does not — the journal identity, submission logistics, and the venue's public self-presentation.

## Source scholarship

The venue's public register: Antikythera "is focused on planetary computation and the evolution of intelligence" and supports "interdisciplinary fundamental research on behalf of a renewed philosophy of technology." The site repeats the brief's concept-lag mandate ("the job of philosophy is not to project ancient axioms onto new circumstances but to actively invent the conceptual systems necessary to grasp the present and orient the future") and its key framings (parasociety, hereditary anthropomorphization, "human-masked ghosts from the future," constraints "psychological, philosophical, linguistic, symbolic, existential") — for argument-facing use of those framings, cite the brief's passage cards, not this page. Distinct to the site: the Agentworld special issue is a peer-reviewed MIT Press journal venue launching Fall 2026; the review window opened June 25, 2026; submissions may be proposals or full drafts (abstract ≤500 words, biography/CV, one work sample); and the venue explicitly invites work exceeding conventional academic formats — "philosophical argument, technical analysis, design research, diagrams, software, infrastructure proposals, visual media, or web-native formats." That last clause is the venue's own licence for this repository's publication-surface approach.

## Essay uses

Venue logistics and the format licence for the submission package; program self-description feeding the R13/R22–R23 calibration and the §5→0 · #2 emblem-return staging. Not an argument-bearing source: claims about agency, parasociety, and the crossover belong to the brief's house.

## Open acquisition and verification
